doc: What a screen shows while it loads from the server: loading, empty, error, ready or refreshing. An error only replaces the screen when there is nothing to show.

state.status: loading | empty | error | ready | refreshing: refreshing still shows the old content
state.error: string | null: the message the error screen shows
state.token: int: the token of the latest fetch; only its result counts
state.fetching: bool: a fetch is in flight
state.refreshByUser: bool: a refresh the user started is in flight; the host shows busy on the control that started it

refresh.byUser: bool: the user started it (a refresh button, pull to refresh); false for a background refresh (refetch on focus or reconnect)

succeeded.empty: bool: the answer has nothing in it

fetch.token: int: fetch, and report the result with this token

notify.id: string: the toast id, notifyId, so repeated failures replace one toast
notify.message: string: a toast, for an error the screen does not show

rules: A screen starts as loading, before any fetch.
start (the screen opens, or what it shows changes, such as another channel) discards what is shown, from any state: loading, the error cleared, a new token and fetch{token}.
refresh while ready keeps the content on screen: refreshing, a new token, refreshByUser set from the event's byUser, and fetch{token}.
refresh while empty keeps the empty screen: still empty, a new token, refreshByUser set from byUser, and fetch{token}.
refresh while error is a retry.
refresh while a fetch is in flight starts no new fetch. A refresh the user started marks the fetch in flight as user-started (refreshByUser), unless the screen is loading.
retry while error loads again: loading, the error cleared, a new token and fetch{token}. retry in any other state does nothing.
succeeded for the current fetch shows the empty screen when the answer is empty, and the content otherwise.
failed for the current fetch while loading, when there is nothing to show, replaces the skeleton with the error screen and its message.

failed for the current fetch during a refresh keeps what is shown (the old content, or the empty screen) and raises notify{id, message} instead, with id the notifyId parameter, so repeated failures replace one toast rather than stacking.
A result with any other token, or one that arrives when no fetch is in flight, does nothing.

refreshByUser is true only while a refresh the user started is in flight, so the host can show busy on the control that started it; a background refresh shows nothing. start, retry and any result clear it.

scenarios.name: an error during a refresh keeps the content
refresh while error is a retry
start discards a fetch in flight
a user refresh shows busy on its control
repeated refresh failures share one toast id
a user refresh while loading stays a load
